analysis:
Both changed files are test-only. EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift has a single changed line at 74: the tinyGemma4Text fixture's config type is now module-qualified (MLXLLM.Gemma4TextConfiguration). This is a name-disambiguation change with no runtime or production effect. EngineV2LivenessRecoveryTests.swift changes the LivenessStubLanguageModel.prepare signature to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks the upstream LanguageModel protocol change in the mlx-swift-lm dependency and touches only a stub. No production source, key custody, attestation, coordinator WebSocket handling, prefix-cache crypto or TTL, or fan helper code is modified.

I also read the unchanged remainder of the gate tests. They assert fail-closed behavior that matches T-041 and the TB-007 posture: the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch disables the cache, packed/legacy resident or tensor prefix construction is refused before any cache I/O, the crash-loop guard degrades only `.auto`, and explicit paged selection refuses rather than silently degrading. The new test-environment default of kvQuantization=native only qualifies existing behavior. Test caches use ephemeral keys in temp directories and do not weaken any production control.

Remaining integration question: the real LanguageModel protocol signature change (state and prefill parameters) lives in the dependency or production sources, which were not supplied here. If that change alters prefill or state handling, such as the new LMOutput.State being carried into cached or paged prefix state, it would need review in its own files. Nothing in this batch shows a security regression.
